body.heading: Start from your real week
paragraphs: Goals copied from someone else's highlight reel often assume free evenings, endless energy and no obligations. When they collide with a real week, we blame ourselves instead of the fit.
Before setting a goal, look honestly at your week: school or work, family, rest, the commitments that are not moving. Then choose a goal that fits into the gaps that genuinely exist.

body.heading: Specific beats impressive
paragraphs: “Get fit” is a wish; “walk for twenty minutes after lunch on weekdays” is a plan. A fitting goal names what you will do, when you will do it, and how you will know it happened.
Small and specific is not a lack of ambition. It is how ambition survives contact with an ordinary Tuesday — and ordinary Tuesdays are where goals are actually won or lost.

takeaway: Choose goals sized for your real life, and they stand a chance.
